pergunta: Does the transfer chain Q1->Q2->Q3->Q4 (Bauru, seed 42, g10b2) breach the b=2km buffer? For each pair (Qi training -> Qi+1 test) -- including the pairs Q1/Q2 and Q3/Q4, which share the same block permutation because they have the same group count -- how many TEST nodes of Qi+1 lie at distance < 2km from TRAINING nodes of Qi, what is the minimum observed distance and what fraction of test nodes is affected?
hipotese: The 2km buffer is applied ONLY within each quadrant (against that quadrant's own training/val); nothing in the protocol trims the test of one quadrant against the training of the geographically neighbouring quadrant. Since the Bauru quadrants are physically adjacent (they share an edge or have a gap of ~1 grid step, ~30m, according to 1.1), a number of violations > 0 is expected if border blocks happen to fall as training-in-Qi and test-in-Qi+1 on the same stretch of boundary; if the cells are sufficiently disjoint/distant (1.1), the result may be 0 -- the number is reported in any case.
limiar_de_aceitacao: 0 test nodes of Qi+1 within 2km of the training of Qi, in the 3 pairs of the chain (Q1->Q2, Q2->Q3, Q3->Q4), with distance computed in global city coordinates (same origin lon0/lat0 for the 2 quadrants of the pair, not the local origin of each graph)
o_que_refuta: any pair with a violation count > 0 refutes the threshold; severity classification: blocks A3/A4 when models are chained across quadrants (triggers phase 4.3 of the roadmap -- retraining without chain or reporting both arms); if 0 in all 3 pairs, the finding is stated in the text with the number (it is not a null test, it is a citable result)
